shortLine: Boundaries: Natural Earth · CShapes 2.0 & CShapes-Europe (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) · historical-basemaps (GPL-3.0). Modified.

boundary.title: Natural Earth 50m
boundary.citation: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data at naturalearthdata.com.
boundary.role: Present-day country identity, the hexagon geometry every current country is drawn from, and the land basemap.
boundary.modifications: Sovereigns dissolved from their map units, overseas units removed, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh.

boundary.title: CShapes 2.0
boundary.citation: Schvitz, Guy, Seraina Rüegger, Luc Girardin, Lars-Erik Cederman, Nils Weidmann, and Kristian Skrede Gleditsch. 2022. “Mapping the International System, 1886-2019: The CShapes 2.0 Dataset.” Journal of Conflict Resolution 66(1): 144-161.
boundary.role: Period-aware historical country boundaries from 1886, and the present-day outlines of Palestine and Zanzibar, which Natural Earth does not carry as separate countries.
boundary.modifications: Selected per country-period, some periods extended or merged to cover a coding unit's own span, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh.

boundary.title: CShapes-Europe
boundary.citation: Cederman, Lars-Erik, Luc Girardin, Carl Müller-Crepon, and Yannick Pengl. 2025. Nationalism and the Transformation of the State: Border Change and Political Violence in the Modern World. Cambridge University Press.
boundary.role: Period-aware European boundaries from 1816, including the pre-unification German and Italian states.
boundary.modifications: Selected per country-period, some periods extended backwards to cover a coding unit's own span, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh.

boundary.title: Historical Basemaps
boundary.role: World snapshots for 1783, 1800 and 1815, used only for the entities and years neither CShapes series reaches.
boundary.modifications: One snapshot year's polygon carried across a span of years, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh. Every polygon taken from a snapshot is graded low confidence for this reason.

boundary.title: Demscore project approximation
boundary.role: A low-confidence marker near Aden so V-Dem's pre-1967 South Yemen values are drawn somewhere honest rather than across the later People's Democratic Republic.
boundary.modifications: Drawn by hand, reprojected and cut into a hexagon mesh like every other polygon.

mapOutput.statement: The hexagon meshes and the map tiles rendered from them are adaptations of CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 boundary data, so they are offered onward under the same licence: attribution, non-commercial use, and share-alike. This deployment is itself non-commercial — no advertising, no paid access and no bundling into a commercial service.
mapOutput.note: A view can mix GPL-3.0 and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 polygons in one image; at 1830, for instance, the map draws both. The image is treated as a mixed-source map: each source stays credited above, and the GPL-3.0 notice travels here.

licenses.text:
The QoG datasets are open and available, free of charge and without a need to register your data. You can use them for your analysis, graphs, teaching, and other academic-related and non-commercial purposes. We ask our users to cite always the original source(s) of the data and our datasets.

We do not allow other uses of these data including but not limited to redistribution, commercialization and other for-profit usage. If a user is interested in such use or has doubts about the license, they will have to refer to the original source and check with them if this is allowed and what requirements they need to fulfill.

Be mindful that the original data sources are the only owners of their data and they can adjust their license without previous warning.

licenses.text: REPDEM presents the comparative data collection efforts undertaken by various research and data infrastructure projects on political institutions, political parties, cabinets and governments in Europe. Repdem offers a range of datasets available for free (without even a demand for registration).
